name: Lady's bedstraw
grown_as: A wild perennial of dry grassland and banks.
habit: A sprawling to upright perennial 15 to 80 cm, many thin wiry four-angled stems, leafy all the way up, topped by a froth of tiny yellow flowers; spreads by creeping stems.

leaf.arrangement: In whorls (rings) of 8 to 12 round the stem, the whorls evenly spaced
leaf.outline: Very narrow, needle-like, 1 to 2.5 cm long and 1 to 2 mm wide
leaf.tip: Ending in a tiny sharp point
leaf.surface: Shiny above, paler and finely hairy beneath

flower.petals: Four lobes, joined at the base, spreading flat, pointed
flower.carried: Hundreds together in dense, branched, frothy clusters at the tops of the stems and in the upper leaf whorls, making a long leafy plume

fruit: Tiny paired smooth round nutlets, about 1 mm, green turning black. The plant dries and blackens after flowering.
seedling: Two small oval seed leaves on short stalks, then the first small whorl of narrow leaves
winter: Dies back to low creeping shoots at the base; old stems turn black-brown.

leaf: needle-like narrow leaves in a whorl of 8 to 12 round the stem
edges rolled under, tiny point at the tip
bloom: many packed into a dense branched cluster
seedling: the first whorl of narrow leaves
young: thin stems with evenly spaced whorls of needle-like leaves
flower: wiry stems with whorls of needle-like leaves
frothy dense plumes of tiny yellow flowers at the top
seedhead: stems turning black-brown with tiny dark paired fruits
dormant: low creeping shoots at the base, old dark stems

look_alikes: Hedge bedstraw (Galium album) has white flowers and broader leaves in whorls of six to eight. Cleavers is sticky and clings, with white flowers. Crosswort (Cruciata laevipes) has four broader hairy leaves in each whorl and yellow flowers in the leaf joints.
